`UnifiedActivationPipeline` in `.aios-core/development/scripts/unified-activation-pipeline.js` is the single entry point for ALL 12 agents; `generate-greeting.js` delegates to `UnifiedActivationPipeline.activate(agentId)`. `GreetingBuilder` assembles greetings; pipeline preloads enriched context. `loadUserProfile()` is called in `buildGreeting()` and passed to `_buildContextualGreeting()` to avoid double `resolveConfig()` calls. `GreetingPreferenceManager.getPreference(userProfile)` accepts optional userProfile for bob restriction; PM bypasses restriction. Bob non-PM: `auto` shows redirect; forced `named` shows simple named greeting.

Pipeline: Phase 1 parallel 5 loaders (`Promise.all`); Phase 2 agent definition; Phase 3 sequential preference/session type/workflow; Phase 4 enriched context; Phase 5 GreetingBuilder. Eight agents use `visibility: [full, quick, key]`; `qa`, `data-engineer`, `devops`, `ux-design-expert` have NO visibility metadata and fall back to first 12 commands. `aios-master` uses `visibility: full`. Bob mode returns empty commands for non-PM. `*yolo` is universal across all 12 agents. Badge: `_safeGetPermissionBadge()` in `greeting-builder.js`.

When mocking `resolveConfig`, use `mockReturnValue` (not `mockReturnValueOnce`) if called multiple times. `validate-user-profile.js` `validateUserProfile()` is pure (no filesystem). Always mock `fs`, `js-yaml`, `config-resolver`, and dependency modules BEFORE requiring the module under test. `resolveConfig()` merges L1-L5; L5 (`user-config.yaml`) has highest priority. `user_profile` is USER_FIELD in `migrate-config.js`; `toggleUserProfile()` in `config-resolver.js` flips bob<->advanced.

`PermissionMode` and `OperationGuard` in `.aios-core/core/permissions/` are fully functional. `cycleMode()` and `enforcePermission()` are wiring in `index.js`. Mode cycle: `explore`(0) -> `ask`(1) -> `auto`(2) -- `PermissionMode.MODE_CYCLE`.

Source `.aios-core/development/agents/`; Claude mirror `.claude/commands/AIOS/agents/`; separate files, synced separately by `ideSync`. Use `fs.writeFile(path, data, { flag: 'wx' })` for exclusive create lock. Include PID + timestamp in lock data; stale ~10s, timeout ~3s, polling 50ms. Use `{path}.tmp.{pid}` + `fs.rename()`; Windows rename failure on existing target falls back to direct `fs.writeFile()`. Cache fingerprint: `.git/HEAD` mtime + `.git/index` mtime. Use `git rev-parse --git-dir` for worktree-aware path and `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to detect worktree/main tree. When `writeFile` serves dual purpose (lock + cache), use broad `mockResolvedValue` and verify via `mock.calls` filtering. Mock `child_process.execSync` separately from `execa`. Use `jest.requireActual('fs')` for real filesystem checks in hook existence tests.

All section builders (`buildPresentation`, `buildRoleDescription`, `buildProjectStatus`, `buildFooter`, `buildContextSection`) accept optional `sectionContext`; `_buildContextualGreeting` creates it from enriched context and passes it to all builders. Present context: named brief greeting for existing/workflow sessions; absent: archetypal backward-compatible fallback. `_formatProjectStatusNarrative()` gives natural sentences; legacy `_formatProjectStatus()` is used without context. `_safeBuildSection(fn)` wraps builders with SECTION_TIMEOUT (150ms) + try/catch. `Promise.all([contextSection, workflowSection])` parallelizes sections. Footer: new `*guide`; existing `*help + *session-info`; workflow `Focused on **{story}**`. ACT-5 changes (lines 661-816 in greeting-builder.js) must NOT be touched -- they own workflow navigator section.

`VerificationGate` at `.aios-core/core/ids/verification-gate.js` uses Template Method; `CircuitBreaker` at `.aios-core/core/ids/circuit-breaker.js` is CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN. Gates G1-G
